transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (Solutions), Emily Reyes (Clearwater - Procurement), Rajiv Menon (Clearwater - GC), Tom Anders (Clearwater - CTO), Lisa Yu (Clearwater - Finance)

Summary: Quick procurement + legal alignment on MSA/DPA exceptions and billing bands. Customer has a white-glove onboarding checklist, wants specific SLA language for latency and uptime for a dedicated pool option, plus clarity on data residency and KMS/HSM for keys. Next steps: redline, docs share, procurement timeline.

Topics: MSA exceptions, DPA retention, SLA / uptime, billing bands and invoicing cadence, KMS/HSM and SSO/SAML, private deployment options (VPC/on-prem), SOC2 artifacts, procurement timeline and PO process.

Action items (captured in header): see metadata.

Transcript body:
00:00 Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. Quick roll call?
00:06 Emily Reyes: Hi this is Emily, procurement, here.
00:08 Rajiv Menon: Rajiv, counsel.
00:10 Tom Anders: Tom, CTO.
00:12 Lisa Yu: Lisa, finance.
00:14 Maya Chen: Maya from Redwood, SE.
00:16 Alex Rivera: Alex here on solutions.
00:18 Jordan Patel: Great, objective for today is to walk through the outstanding MSA exceptions, DPA clauses, and the billing model so procurement knows the path to sign. We'll also cover security artifacts briefly. Should take about 45 minutes to an hour. Sound good?
00:29 Emily Reyes: Yep sounds good. We have a procurement window -- our internal deadline is May 20th so we need to get legal and finance comfortable before then.
00:36 Rajiv Menon: I have a short list of exceptions, mostly around indemnity cap and data residency language in the DPA. Also need more specifics on audit logs and KMS integration.
00:46 Jordan Patel: Ok understood. On our side we typically accept a mutual indemnity with a standard cap tied to annual spend, open to aligning on a fixed cap or a multiple, which we can discuss. Want me to pull up the MSA doc?
00:59 Tom Anders: If I can jump in, from infra side we care about the service levels for burst capacity and also how emergency fallbacks work if a region has issues. We may want a dedicated capacity pool or a private VPC deployment.
01:12 Maya Chen: To be clear, there are three patterns: hosted API (fastest), dedicated reserved pools (predictable throughput), and private deployments (VPC or on-prem). Dedicated gives predictable load and helps with per-request latency, but cost is higher. Private/VPC lets you control network egress rules and KMS.
01:31 Rajiv Menon: On KMS, we need to know if Redwood can support customer-managed keys via HSM or cloud KMS, and whether keys reside in our KMS only or somewhere else.
01:43 Maya Chen: We support customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS providers; there is an HSM-backed option for Private deployments. For hosted we can integrate with your KMS via a secure proxy, but if you require full key custody we recommend Private. I'll share the spec doc after the call.
01:57 Lisa Yu: For billing we need a clear model: monthly committed, overage rates, and PO invoicing cadence. We also need examples with numbers.
02:06 Jordan Patel: Absolutely. We usually propose a committed monthly for Dedicated with a unit price and then a per-token overage. For hosted customers it's pay-as-you-go. I can send a sample invoice and pricing band table.
02:18 Emily Reyes: Also need to validate if the DPA has a data deletion SLA and specific retention periods for logs and transcripts.
02:25 Maya Chen: In our standard DPA we have retention windows for customer content and separate logs. We can add a clause for deletion within X days post-contract termination, open to a 30/90 day window, but need to check with ops for longer archival needs.
02:40 Rajiv Menon: We typically require 90 days and a certificate of deletion for regulated data.
02:48 Maya Chen: Noted. We'll flag that as an exception to discuss in the redline.
02:53 Jordan Patel: On the SLA side, do you have specific uptime or latency SLOs you want spelled out?
03:00 Tom Anders: We have internal SLAs: 99.95% uptime for critical endpoints and p95 latency targets under 200ms for conversational flows. If you can offer dedicated capacity with pinned model versions, that helps us meet the p95.
03:16 Maya Chen: 99.95% is achievable for dedicated+redundant regions with SLA credits. For p95 200ms, that depends on model and sequence length; smaller models meet that more consistently. We can propose a guaranteed latency band for a specified model class plus credits if breached. Also note that private on-prem will more easily meet latency since it's on your network.
03:36 Emily Reyes: Is the latency SLA in the MSA or an addendum?
03:40 Jordan Patel: Typically it's an SLA addendum tied to the service seat / dedicated commit. We'll provide the exact verification and credit language.
03:47 Rajiv Menon: On encryption in transit and at rest we need confirmation for TLS versions and the storage encryption. And how audit logs are retained and accessible for our auditors.
03:56 Maya Chen: TLS 1.2+ standard, data at rest encrypted with AES-256. For hosted, logs are available via console and can be exported; for Private we can ship logs to your SIEM via secure forwarding. We also provide audit log entries for admin actions.
04:12 Tom Anders: One subtlety — our security team will want to run a pen test and possibly a code scan against any connectors you ship for private deployments. Is that supported?
04:21 Maya Chen: Yes, we do allow customer pen testing under a test window and there's a standard process. We'll coordinate with security to provide scope and schedule.
04:29 Jordan Patel: Ok let's go through Rajiv's redline list. Rajiv, can you summarize top three legal sticking points?
04:34 Rajiv Menon: Sure: 1) indemnity cap and carve-outs for IP; 2) DPA deletion timeframe and audit rights; 3) liability allocation in case of model hallucination leading to regulated harm.
04:46 Jordan Patel: On indemnity cap, are you seeking a fixed number or a multiplier of fees?
04:50 Rajiv Menon: Prefer a multiple of twelve months of fees as a starting point, but willing to discuss for critical regulated data exposures.
04:58 Jordan Patel: We can propose a compromise; Jordan to propose options in the redline.
05:02 Emily Reyes: For procurement flow: once we have redline and security artifacts, we expect a procurement packet for our board approval. That includes sample SOW, pricing, and a lead time for onboarding.
05:15 Lisa Yu: Lead time impacts cash planning; please flag any minimum commit months for discounts.
05:20 Jordan Patel: Understood — we'll include both monthly committed and annual commit examples.
05:25 Alex Rivera: I'll also include an onboarding checklist with tasks split between teams and expected time estimates for Dedicated vs Private.
05:33 Tom Anders: Regarding data residency, we need to ensure that customer content for EU customers remains in eu-west region. How does Redwood guarantee region pinning?
05:44 Maya Chen: We support region pinning for both hosted and dedicated. For hosted, we can pin the tenant to a region; for private you control physical location. There is a small delay for failover to another region unless explicitly configured. We'll add language in the runbook.
05:58 Rajiv Menon: About audit logs and e-discovery — can Redwood provide a legally-signed export of logs?
06:06 Maya Chen: We can provide exports and a formal attestation in Private deployments; for hosted, we provide exports and timestamped logs, and we can work with legal on format and signatures.
06:16 Emily Reyes: One more billing nuance: we prefer net-60 invoicing and a PO up front. Does Redwood accept net-60?
06:24 Jordan Patel: Standard is net-30 but enterprise can do net-45/60 on contract. Need to get finance sign-off. Jordan to confirm and include in redline.
06:33 Lisa Yu: Also specify currency and tax handling. We'll be invoiced in USD but need VAT handling for EU entities.
06:39 Jordan Patel: Noted.
06:41 Tom Anders: A technical point: if we run a pilot, do you allow a temporary lower commit or a pilot credit? We want to test latency under load.
06:50 Jordan Patel: Yes typically we run a pilot with limited credits and a scoped test harness. Maya can run the benchmark and provide the results.
06:57 Maya Chen: I'll propose a benchmark test plan: sequence lengths, concurrency patterns, and synthetic user profiles. We'll need a test dataset (sanitized) and a runbook.
07:08 Tom Anders: Ok, that covers most of the ask. Rajiv, any more legal queries?
07:12 Rajiv Menon: One last ask: escrow and survival clauses for critical model weights if you ever shut down?
07:18 Jordan Patel: For model IP we can discuss escrow for closed-source components; for open models it's different. I'll note this as a potential term to chat with product/legal.
07:26 Emily Reyes: Can we talk about who signs — signature authority? Our procurement needs a named exec with signing rights.
07:31 Lisa Yu: For our org, CFO or Head of Legal typically signs above threshold. We'll confirm in the procurement packet.
07:38 Jordan Patel: Great. Let's talk timeline — when do you think procurement can approve?
07:43 Emily Reyes: If we get the redline by Friday (May 8) and security artifacts by Monday (May 11), we can route for approval and aim for a May 20 sign.
07:55 Jordan Patel: Sounds good. I'll aim to send the redline by EOD May 8.
07:59 Alex Rivera: I'll upload the onboarding checklist and sample SOW link to the shared folder after call.
08:04 Tom Anders: Quick question — any competitors on your side being compared? We saw Anthropic and BigCloud AI in our RFP. Anything Redwood calls out versus them?
08:12 Jordan Patel: We tend to differentiate on production tooling, cost controls, and private deployment parity. We can put together a short comparison doc.
08:21 Rajiv Menon: On DPA, if you can accept a 90-day deletion and certificate, that addresses a big concern.
08:28 Maya Chen: We'll confirm with ops and push that in the redline.
08:33 Emily Reyes: Ok if we agree to next steps I can start procurement paperwork as soon as the redline lands.
08:38 Jordan Patel: Recap: Jordan will send redlined MSA/DPA with options for indemnity cap and net-60 ask; Maya to circulate SOC2 artifacts, KMS/HSM integration doc, network topology and pen test process; Alex to share onboarding checklist and sample SOW; Lisa to send expected monthly usage bands; Emily to confirm procurement timeline May 20.
08:59 Tom Anders: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
09:02 Jordan Patel: Thanks all. We'll follow up with links in the email.

References/links mentioned (will be shared post-call):
- SOC2 summary + artifact list (to be shared by Maya)
- Network topology & KMS integration spec (to be shared)
- Sample invoice and pricing bands spreadsheet (to be shared)
- Onboarding checklist & SOW template (Alex to share)

Notes about transcript quality: occasional speaker overlap and minor transcription errors (product name sometimes transcribed as "Readwood" or "Redwoode").
